newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen continuing lower at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen continuing lower at open.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to open lower on Wednesday, continuing Tuesday's downtrend, as investors watch and wait ahead of U.S. economic data.

"We'll probably see more of what we saw yesterday in Canada, and that is off.... we have to sit and wait for the economic stuff to come out and that will really tell us which way the day is going," one trader said.

U.S. wholesale inventories and sales for March and preliminary first quarter non-farm productivity and costs are due out at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. March consumer credit data is to be released at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 20.76 to finish at 6129.96 on Tuesday during the second heaviest trading session ever.
Traders said dealings in controversial gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd would likely be busy for a few more days before fading permanently.
"For all intents and purposes it is over, the volume will probably decline dramatically over the next week and a half or so," one trader said. Bre-X resumed on Tuesday after

Monday's all-day halt after a report revealed its Busang gold find was an outright fraud instead of the world's largest gold discovery. The stock lost nearly all of its value and ended the day down 3.145 to 0.085 in 58.3 million shares.
((Andrea Hopkins at Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8102 or e-mail andrea.hopkins@reuters.com))
